QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_29

question.text: Under the catch-up provision described in the Cat III AIF workbook, after investors have received their capital contribution and the Preferred Return (hurdle), how are the residual profits distributed?

answer.text: Entirely to investors on a pro-rata basis
First to the Investment Manager up to the agreed catch-up amount, and any further residual returns are then split between investors and the Manager in the agreed ratio
Entirely to the Investment Manager up to the Performance Fees rate
Only to investors with committed capital above INR 10 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines the Catch-up Rate as the rate at which residual profits, after returning investors' capital and the hurdle return, are distributed to the Manager so the Manager can "catch up" to the pre-determined share of total profits (typically 10–20%). From the additional returns generated over and above the hurdle, the Manager is first paid the agreed catch-up amount; thereafter, the residual additional returns are distributed in the agreed ratio between investors and the Manager. The Trap: Option A ignores the catch-up step entirely. Option C overstates the Manager's share by skipping the residual split. Option D invents a commitment-size eligibility rule that is not in the source. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II AIF Managers) tests the same hurdle + catch-up mechanic in close-ended fund structures.
